intro.author: Micah of Moresheth (1:1), a small town in Judah's lowland hills
intro.written: Late 700s BC, in the reigns of Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah of Judah
intro.audience: Judah and Jerusalem, with warnings also to Samaria and the northern kingdom
intro.setting: Micah was a contemporary of Isaiah. He saw Assyria destroy Samaria in 722 BC and sweep through Judah's towns in 701 BC. As a man from the countryside, he denounced Jerusalem's leaders for seizing farmers' land and perverting justice, while still promising a future ruler from Bethlehem.
intro.purpose: To expose injustice and false religion, announce judgment on Samaria and Jerusalem, and hold out hope of a faithful remnant and a shepherd-king who brings peace.
intro.bigIdea: God requires us 'to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly' with him, and he delights in mercy.

outline.title: Judgment on Samaria and Judah, and a remnant gathered
Corrupt leaders, Zion's future, and a ruler from Bethlehem
God's case against his people, and his pardoning love
